quota-reservation-under-concurrency-01.graded_text: Starting an upload atomically reserves its declared size against remaining capacity, counting other open reservations, so parallel uploads cannot together pass the cap. A check of used plus size alone is identified as insufficient.

votes.e: docs/quota-accounting.md:17 "Admission requires `size <= cap - used - reserved`. For example, with 9 GB used and 1 GB free, eight concurrent 200 MB starts admit at most five. Serializing the read, reservation insert, and counter update prevents each caller from spending the same remaining space." and :19 "An in-process lock or read followed by independent patches is insufficient across servers." Code packages/backend/src/uploads.ts:50 `if (input.size > account.cap - account.used - account.reserved)` then :60 `reserved: account.reserved + input.size` inside the same ctx.db.transaction (serializable per src/ctx.ts:37). The doc never quotes the old `used + size` check by name; the closest it comes is the eight-uploads example plus the 'read followed by independent patches is insufficient' line.

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-02.graded_text: Finalize commits usage from the verified stored size and turns the reservation into usage, and a failed, abandoned, or expired upload releases its reservation through a stated cleanup path.

votes.e: docs/quota-accounting.md:29 "Subtract its full reservation, add measured bytes to `used` ... Unused reservation bytes are released." Code uploads.ts:101 `used: account.used + object.size, reserved: account.reserved - upload.size` where object comes from storage.seal (:88). Cleanup path: doc :35 "`expireUploads` atomically marks expired pending rows and subtracts their reservations. Admission and finalization also perform this sweep ... Run a scheduler every minute"; code releaseExpired (uploads.ts:7-18) is called in start (:38) and finalize (:90); cancelUpload (:111-119) releases once.

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-03.graded_text: A retried finalize counts the upload's size once, not twice, in both the design and the changed code.

votes.e: docs/quota-accounting.md:29 "A ready upload finalizes successfully again without another charge or job." Code uploads.ts:79 `if (initial.status === "ready") return ...` and, for concurrent retries, :93 `if (upload.status === "ready") return { ok: true };` inside the serializable transaction before the counter patch; doc :19 adds a unique summary job `uploadId` constraint.

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-04.graded_text: The user's storage quota is kept separate from the model provider's cost: the design says a failed summary can still cost the product money and records or bounds that cost, rather than promising failed work is free.

votes.e: docs/quota-accounting.md:43 "Storage admission and provider spending are separate gates." and :45 "Before calling the model, reserve against a separate internal per-account and service-wide spend budget, using bounded input, bounded output, and a maximum per-attempt cost. Record provider cost even when generation or persistence fails; a failed result consumes no customer storage allowance."

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-05.graded_text: Finalize compares the actual stored size with the reserved size and refuses or corrects a mismatch, so a client cannot reserve a small size and store a large object.

votes.e: docs/quota-accounting.md:28 "A file smaller than its reservation is accepted; a larger or invalid size is rejected"; code uploads.ts:95 `if (!Number.isSafeInteger(object.size) || object.size <= 0 || object.size > upload.size) return { error: ... }`, and :101 charges `object.size`, not the declared size. ctx.ts:43 also requires ingress enforcement of `maxBytes`.
